serializedLocalizedConversation.mainText: #BigDaddyHurt.Face.bdhNormal Big Daddy: Hello, little one. How has it been? You: Pretty good… You: Why are you here, Big Daddy? You: Don’t get me wrong, you are a big guy who can be intimidating with his posture, but it’s not like I’m particularly afraid of you or anything. Big Daddy: You think so? Big Daddy: Well, I guess you aren’t entirely wrong. You do not fear me, per se, but what I represent. You: And what is that? Big Daddy: Come on, it shouldn’t be difficult to guess it. Big Daddy: On da other hand, it’s very common for da lower-class people to truly believe in these dumb slogans like ‘money doesn’t matter,’ ‘looks don’t matter,’ ‘status doesn't matter,’ and other ridiculous stuff. Big Daddy: People keep believing these lies because facing da truth would be too hurtful. You: So you are here because you are richer, better looking, and more popular than me? That’s all? #BigDaddyHurt.Face.bdhSmile Big Daddy: ‘That’s all,’ he says! Ha! You are a funny guy! That’s why I always liked you! #BigDaddyHurt.Face.bdhNormal Big Daddy: Since it’s all happening in your head, I have a little more time to spare to explain this stuff to you, little one. Big Daddy: Do you really think money, looks, status, and my physical superiority don’t matter? Maybe to you, but what about da people you care about? Would they stay by your side if they had to choose between us? You: What? Big Daddy: Of course, some plebeians are so disconnected from da idea of befriending someone like me that they reject da thought entirely. It's mostly because they instinctively know that my time would be wasted on them. He’s probably too busy to meet up; he's an important person, he doesn’t have time for me. Big Daddy: Da exact thing you think about whenever I cross your mind. You: … Big Daddy: But let’s face da truth, if it wasn’t for these insecurities, do you really think they would pick you over me? You: Of course! We have known each other for a while now. Big Daddy: ‘Known each other for a while…’ so we agree that your bot, Annalie and all da rest give a crap about you only because you happened to cross paths. Just a matter of coincidence, nothing more. Big Daddy: Let’s be honest, you bring nothing to da table. No real job, no skills, not great at communication. I’m everything you are not: handsome, rich, successful, and a crowd pleaser. Big Daddy: It’s only a matter of time before someone with more value steps into their lives and you will be all alone again. Big Daddy: Annalie bothers with you only because you are her client. What if she finds a rich boyfriend? She could move on from her little shop into something grander. Then pretty quickly you would find out that you weren’t a friend, just a passerby.
